g.text: DSCOVR keeps station on the Sun–Earth line, so it follows Earth around the Sun and sees one turn per solar day. An observer fixed among the stars would see the sidereal day, 236 s shorter: 11 frequency-resolution elements

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781
